title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.10-11). G is an algebraic group over Q, and ω is the fibre functor on C = Rep(G). A 'G-subordination' F on an analytic base S is a ⊗-functor Rep(G) → Hodge(S), i.e. a variation of Hodge structure whose Mumford–Tate group is 'subordinate to' G. Equivalently it is a VHS with G-structure, possibly with an implicit compatibility with ω. For each s, P_s = Isom_⊗(ω, L_s∘F) is a torsor under Γ = G(Q). These glue to a principal Γ-covering P → S. Pulling F back to P trivialises the underlying local system, and the result is a 'rigidified' G-subordination. This gives a Γ-equivariant classifying map g : P → 𝒴, where 𝒴 is the space of Hodge structures on ω with G-structure: a G(R)-orbit/period-type domain. Hence G-subordinations on S are the same as pairs (P, g) with P a principal Γ-covering and g a Γ-morphism.

This page introduces level structures. Fix Γ_0 ⊂ Γ = G(Q), preferably commensurable with G(Z), i.e. arithmetic. A Γ_0-rigidified G-subordination on S is a principal covering P_0 → S with group Γ_0, together with a Γ_0-equivariant morphism P_0 → 𝒴. The two extreme cases are:
- Γ_0 = {e}: rigidified G-subordinations, classified by 𝒴 itself.
- Γ_0 = G(Q): plain G-subordinations.
Equivalently, one gives F compatible with ω plus a reduction of the Γ_S-torsor P to a Γ_{0,S}-subtorsor P_0 ⊂ P. That is a level-Γ_0 structure, exactly as for level structures on abelian varieties.

The moduli problem then has a classifying ('modular') topos: the topos of Γ_0-equivariant sheaves on 𝒴, i.e. the quotient stack [𝒴/Γ_0] (Γ_0 acting on the right). When Γ_0 acts properly discontinuously as a discrete group, the naive quotient Γ_0\𝒴 is an analytic space. It 'plays the role of a moduli variety of level Γ_0'. In modern terms this is a Mumford–Tate / Griffiths period-domain quotient, which is a Shimura variety in the Hermitian case.

Purpose: build moduli spaces for Hodge-theoretic realisations of motives with prescribed motivic Galois group G. This goes in the direction of modular varieties attached to (G, Hodge data).
errors: Properness of the Γ_0-action on 𝒴 needs extra data. A polarization is required, so that 𝒴 is an open G(R)-orbit with compact isotropy, a period domain. Without polarization the space of Hodge structures on ω is not acted on properly by arithmetic groups. Grothendieck's hedge 'quand Γ_0 agit proprement' covers this, but the condition is not stated.

The quotient Γ_0\𝒴 is in general only an analytic space (orbifold if Γ_0 has torsion). By Griffiths' later results it is not algebraic unless the domain is Hermitian symmetric and the Hodge type is of Shimura type. So calling it a 'variété de modules' is only correct in the Shimura case. Also, families from geometry satisfy Griffiths transversality, which is not encoded on this page: the moduli of all G-subordinations versus horizontal maps is not distinguished here.

ideas.what: Level-Γ_0 structure on a G-valued VHS, defined as a reduction of the G(Q)-torsor of ω-trivialisations to a Γ_0-subtorsor
ideas.modern_name: level structure / arithmetic subgroup level on VHS with G-structure; Shimura datum with level K
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971; Variétés de Shimura 1979); Mumford (1966, 1969) for Hodge/Mumford–Tate groups

ideas.what: Moduli topos of Γ_0-rigidified G-subordinations is the Γ_0-equivariant topos of the classifying space 𝒴, i.e. the quotient stack [𝒴/Γ_0]
ideas.modern_name: quotient analytic stack / orbifold [Γ_0\D] as moduli stack of VHS with level structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore after Deligne–Mumford stacks (1969); Carlson–Müller-Stach–Peters textbook treatment
ideas.where_published: Classifying topos of an equivariant space appears in SGA4 in general form, but not for Hodge moduli

ideas.what: Γ_0\𝒴 as an analytic moduli variety of level Γ_0 for Hodge structures with G-structure
ideas.modern_name: Mumford–Tate domain quotient / Griffiths period domain quotient; Shimura variety in Hermitian case
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (1968-70), Deligne (1971/79), Green–Griffiths–Kerr (2012) for Mumford–Tate domains

ideas.what: Equivalence of G-subordinations with pairs (principal Γ-covering P, Γ-equivariant period map g : P → 𝒴)
ideas.modern_name: period map as equivariant map from the monodromy covering to the period domain

missed.claim: In 1965, before Griffiths' period domains (1968) and Deligne's Shimura-variety formalism (1971/79), Grothendieck sets up moduli of Hodge realisations with a prescribed (motivic Galois) group G, with arithmetic level Γ_0 ⊂ G(Q). He gives a stack/topos-theoretic quotient [𝒴/Γ_0] as the moduli object. This is essentially the Mumford–Tate-domain / Shimura-variety picture tied explicitly to the motivic Galois group, which the literature credits to Deligne.
missed.quote: Pour cette structure, il y a un topos modulaire, qui n'est autre que 𝒴_{Γ_0} … joue le rôle d'une variété de modules de niveau Γ_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it shows the motivic-Galois-group programme already contained the idea of Shimura-type moduli as classifying stacks for G-valued Hodge structures with level. This anticipates Deligne's interpretation of Shimura varieties as moduli of motives/Hodge structures with G-structure.

missed.claim: The page does not address when Γ_0\𝒴 is algebraic, nor the role of polarization and transversality. The program stops at the analytic quotient.
missed.quote: quand Γ_0 agit proprement comme un groupe discret
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are exactly the issues resolved later (Griffiths transversality, Griffiths–Robles–Toledo non-algebraicity, Bakker–Klingler–Tsimerman o-minimal definability). Nothing here is new beyond priority.

deep.surprise_reason: Early (1965) and explicit formulation of level-Γ_0 moduli of G-valued Hodge structures as an equivariant topos, with arithmetic quotient as moduli variety. It anticipates Mumford–Tate domains and Shimura varieties as moduli. However, the ideas are now standard and credited to Griffiths and Deligne, and the page is sketchy, so this is mainly of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: First line should read roughly 'groupe Γ_0, et d'un morphisme [Γ_0-équivariant] de P_0 → 𝒴' (continuing 'rev. principal P_0 de S de groupe Γ_0'). It is not 'qui sur Γ_0', and the target is the same curly 𝒴 as on the previous page, not 𝒯.
'𝒯' throughout should be '𝒴', the classifying space g : P → 𝒴 from the previous page.
'qui n'est autre que 𝒯_{/Γ_0}' should be read as 'qui n'est autre que 𝒴_{Γ_0}' (the topos of 𝒴 with Γ_0-action), with a crossed-out preliminary version.
'quand Γ_0 agit proprement comme il se doit discret' should be read as 'quand Γ_0 agit proprement comme un groupe discret'.
'est pour le rôle d'une variété' should be read as 'joue le rôle d'une variété de modules de niveau Γ_0'.
'une sous-fibre P_0 de P' is more likely 'un sous-faisceau P_0 de P', which is a Γ_{0S}-torseur.
